subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw solve this crash-loop with a fixed managed-service heap default now, require a CLI/config heap tuning surface first, or move the mitigation to Node CLI arguments instead of generated service `NODE_OPTIONS`?
rationale: Current code lacks the mitigation, but the fix changes managed service startup defaults and intersects the host-env security policy, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security shape alone.

options.title: Accept fixed default now
options.body: Land or revise the open candidate as the emergency managed-service heap mitigation, then track durable tuning separately if needed.

options.title: Require tunable surface
options.body: Pause the current candidate until maintainers choose and test a `--heap-mb`, config, or other durable operator-controlled surface.

options.title: Require CLI-arg shape
options.body: Use a Node argv `--max-old-space-size` injection instead of generated service `NODE_OPTIONS` if maintainers want to avoid that env key entirely.

recommendation.title: Accept fixed default now
recommendation.body: Land or revise the open candidate as the emergency managed-service heap mitigation, then track durable tuning separately if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent daemon install/service history and broader startup-default work make this the strongest routing candidate for the product-shape decision.
